short: A working astronomer who inherited an empire and lasted two years on the throne.
full:
Timur's grandson was made governor of Samarkand in 1409, at fifteen, and left largely to himself while his father Shah Rukh ruled from Herat. He used the forty years that followed to build a madrasa on the Registan, finished in 1420 and teaching mathematics and astronomy, and then an observatory, and to gather the best mathematicians in the Islamic world — Qadi Zada al-Rumi, Jamshid al-Kashi, Ali Qushji. The resulting star catalogue, the Zij-i Sultani, fixed the positions of over a thousand stars from fresh observation and gave the length of the sidereal year with an error of under a minute.

He succeeded his father in March 1447 and was quickly out of his depth. Khorasan was lost, the Uzbeks raided across the Syr Darya, and in 1449 his own son Abdal-Latif defeated him in the field. Ulugh Beg abdicated and was given leave to make the pilgrimage to Mecca; a court issued a fatwa and he was beheaded on the road on 27 October 1449. Abdal-Latif was murdered six months later.
